about:
Phish-Tac-Toe

Three boards, nine songs each. A square lights up when Phish plays that song tonight. First to three in a row — across, down or diagonal — wins. If more than one board completes a line, the winner is whoever's line finished earlier in the show, which the app works out from the actual setlist order.

Why these 25 songs

Every setlist Phish played in 1995 (83 shows) and every show since Jan 2023 (164 shows) was pulled from the Phantasy Tour API. Each candidate got two numbers: how core it was to 1995, and how often the band still plays it. The score blends them, weighted 0.4 / 0.8 — meaning current rotation actually matters a bit more than era authenticity.

Everything already played is gone

Phish doesn't repeat inside a run. Nights 1–3 (1992, 1993, 1994) burned 66 songs, including 20 of the 30 most-played songs of 1995 — Stash, Reba, Bowie, Antelope, Maze, Chalk Dust, Harry Hood, Sample in a Jar. That's 62% of the probability weight already spent, which is exactly why night 4 is more predictable than night 1 was. Tweezer would have ranked #3 tonight if they hadn't burned it Saturday.

Does the model actually work?

It was backtested against this run's first three nights — scoring each night with that year's own play rates, and excluding whatever the earlier nights had used. It put about half of each night's real setlist in its top picks, against roughly 17% for guessing at random. The percentages on the squares are calibrated: squares marked 30% hit about 30% of the time in that test.

The center square

You Enjoy Myself is the center of all three boards on purpose. It's the one monster left unburned — the 21-minute centerpiece of A Live One, Phish's 1995 album — and the model ranked it a top pick on all three previous nights and was wrong every time. They are saving it. Making it shared means nobody gets an unfair edge from the single most likely song, and all three boards light up together when it drops.

Fairness

The other 24 songs were assigned by an optimizer that enumerated all 512 states of each board exactly. All three boards came out at a 50.4–50.5% chance of three-in-a-row and 4.04–4.06 expected hits. Nobody has the better board. There's an 84% chance somebody wins.

If the feed lags

The setlist comes from Phantasy Tour, updated by fans during the show, and is re-checked about every 30 seconds. If it falls behind, hit Manual entry and mark squares yourself — those marks stay on your own phone and can only add hits, never remove one.

Odds are one model's opinion, not gospel. Phish will do whatever Phish wants. That's the entire point.
